label: GO after a rewarded visit to S2, about to choose a2 (early in the episode only)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), when the reward input is 1 (previous trial rewarded), the previous trial reached S2 (prev_state -1 = first trial of the window, where history is not in the window), and the agent is choosing a2 (model_act == 2; strongly negative choice logit). It is silent after a1/S1 rewards and after any unrewarded trial. It also has a strong time-in-episode dependence: active on trials ~0-40 and completely silent from ep_trial ~45 onward, so ep_trial < 40 is part of the predicate (dev F1 0.94, mass recall 0.99; ep_trial < 38 gives F1 0.945). Magnitude is largest at the first rewarded-S2 GO in a run and decays over subsequent repeated a2-rewarded GO steps (e.g. 1.0 -> 0.69 -> 0.39), and the activation is concentrated where value is high (7.7-8.1). Recorded the model_act version (agent own upcoming choice, legitimate) rather than action == 2 (equivalent at GO). Not fired on: a1 choices, unrewarded previous trials, late-episode trials.

issues: The claims check out on test. The unit never fires outside GO (phase != GO: precision 0, recall 0). It never fires after an unrewarded trial ((GO & ep<40 & a2 & prev_reward==0): 0 of 30529 steps active). It never fires after a rewarded S1 visit (0 of 4724). It almost never fires when the agent chooses a1 (precision 0.056).

The cutoff in ep_trial is a gradual fade, not a sharp switch. Predicate precision by ep_trial bin: <20: 0.98, 20-40: 0.84, 30-35: 0.92, 35-40: 0.57, 40-45: 0.14, >=40 overall: 0.011. So 'completely silent from about 45 on' is roughly right, but 'active on 0 to about 40' hides that trials 35-40 are only about half active. This is the main source of false positives, and a cutoff of 38 tightens it (see below).

Small structure inside the predicate: when the previous rewarded S2 visit was a rare transition (prev_action==1, a1 -> S2), precision is 0.72, against 0.93 when it was common (a2 -> S2). That case covers only 3% of recall, so it is minor. The prev_state==-1 branch (first trial of the window) has precision 0.89, which is acceptable.

Misses hold only 0.8% of the activation mass. They are weak activations at GO with a2 just past the cutoff, or after windows where the state history is ambiguous. They are scattered, not a systematic class.

Choice logit < -2 works as well as model_act == 2 (test F1 0.946 vs 0.947), which agrees with the explanation's point that the agent's own upcoming choice is what matters. No future random variable is involved.
